findings.problem: SensorWorkflow has no typestate enum or state machine; any combination of status string, validated boolean, and sent boolean is allowed, including logically impossible states like is_sent=false with status="sent".
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct a SensorWorkflow with contradictory lifecycle markers, making downstream logic silently incorrect and impossible to reason about statically.
findings.fix: Define a SensorState enum (e.g. Unvalidated, Validated, Sent) that owns the lifecycle. Replace status, is_validated, is_sent, and sent_at_epoch_ms with a single SensorState field. Smart constructor validates initial state.

findings.problem: status is pub status: String, allowing any arbitrary string value ("sent", "SENT", "sentry", "", "deleted") to represent the workflow state instead of a closed set of domain states.
findings.failure_mode: Pattern matching on status is impossible; string comparison is error-prone and case-sensitive; callers can set status to any value breaking all lifecycle invariants without compile-time detection.
findings.fix: Replace pub status: String with a domain enum: pub status: SensorStatus where enum variants encode the lifecycle stages. Match on enum variants instead of string comparison.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool encode lifecycle state as independent flags. These two booleans plus the status string create 2^2 * N possible combinations, most of which are invalid (e.g. validated=false, sent=true, status="sent").
findings.failure_mode: mark_sent only sets is_sent=true and status="sent" but never touches is_validated, leaving the struct in a state where sent=true but validated=false. Callers cannot enforce ordering without runtime checks.
findings.fix: Consolidate is_validated and is_sent into a single enum with ordered variants (Unvalidated -> Validated -> Sent). Transition functions return the next enum variant or a typed error, making invalid transitions a compile-time impossibility.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a separate field from the lifecycle booleans. It can be Some(timestamp) while is_sent=false, or None while is_sent=true, representing logically impossible states that the type system cannot prevent.
findings.failure_mode: Code checking is_sent cannot trust that sent_at_epoch_ms is Some, and code checking sent_at_epoch_ms is Some cannot trust is_sent is true. Both must do runtime double-checks, and even then the state could be inconsistent between checks.
findings.fix: Move the timestamp into the typestate enum variant that owns it: e.g. Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }. Only the Sent variant carries the timestamp, making it impossible for the timestamp to exist without the sent state.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain semantics. Any string is a valid ID, including empty strings, strings with whitespace, or strings that are not identifiers at all.
findings.failure_mode: Downstream code cannot assume the id is a valid sensor identifier. Empty IDs, duplicate IDs, or malformed IDs pass through without validation, leading to silent data corruption or lookup failures.
findings.fix: Define a newtype: pub struct SensorId(String) or better pub struct SensorId { inner: NonEmptyString }. Provide a smart constructor that validates the id format and returns a typed error. Use the newtype everywhere instead of bare String.

findings.problem: Raw primitives cross the parse boundary without fallible smart constructors: SensorWorkflow accepts String id, String status, and bare bools directly. No constructor validates or constrains input at the boundary, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly.
findings.failure_mode: Every caller bypasses validation entirely. mark_sent mutates status and is_sent without checking preconditions (e.g. must be validated before sent). The parse boundary that should turn hostile/untrusted input into trusted domain values is absent.
findings.fix: Add SensorWorkflow::new(id: &str, ...) -> Result<SensorWorkflow, ParseError> as a fallible smart constructor. Add SensorWorkflow::transition_to_sent(self) -> Result<SensorWorkflow, TransitionError> that enforces preconditions. Replace pub fields with a private struct and pub-only constructors.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent or SensorWorkflow lifecycle transitions
no profiler evidence that typestate enum vs bool+string approach is measured for any performance claim
no allocation evidence: status.to_string() allocates on every mark_sent call; no try_reserve or bounded allocation analysis
no command evidence: no cargo clippy, cargo check, or cargo test run against this crate
residual_risk: The entire domain model is represented as raw primitives with no type-driven invariants. Six independent fields allow O(2^3 * N) invalid states where only a linear lifecycle chain is valid. No smart constructors, no typestate enum, no parse boundary. This is a structural architectural violation that cannot be patched incrementally; the type system must be restructured to make illegal states unrepresentable.
